title: The Web Centipede: Understanding How Web Communities Influence Each Other Through the Lens of Mainstream and Alternative News Sources
screen_reason: Large-scale observational measurement of platform data (Twitter 1% stream, all Reddit posts and comments via Pushshift, all 4chan posts on /pol/, /sp/, /int/, /sci/; 30 June 2016 - 28 February 2017) counting posts that carry URLs from a curated list of 54 'alternative' news domains built from Wikipedia's List of fake news websites and FakeNewsWatch plus rt.com and sputniknews.com. Table 1 gives, for each platform, the percentage of ALL crawled posts containing such a URL, with the total post count as denominator - a share of shared items from a source-reliability list, i.e. SHARING (content_share). The bulk of the paper (Hawkes-process influence estimation, propagation sequences) is not prevalence and is not extracted; the paper is not a classifier/detection study.

estimates.misinfo_def: "Using large social networks like Twitter and Facebook, misleading, false, or agenda-driven information can quickly and seamlessly spread online, deceiving people or influencing their opinions"; operationally the alternative list is drawn from "Wikipedia [List of fake news websites] and FakeNewsWatch", plus "two state-sponsored alternative news domains: sputniknews.com and rt.com, as they have recently attracted public attention due to their posting of controversial, and seemingly agenda-pushing stories".
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Source-list classification with no item coding and no reliability statistics: "we create a list of 99 news sites including 45 mainstream and 54 alternative ones"; mainstream = 45 of the Alexa top 100 news sites after dropping user-generated-content, specialised (e.g. finance) and non-English sites; alternative = sites from Wikipedia's List of fake news websites and FakeNewsWatch, plus rt.com and sputniknews.com added by the authors. In the Twitter data the alternative bucket is dominated by breitbart.com (46.04% of alternative URLs), rt.com (17.56%) and infowars.com (17.25%).

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: (a) The alternative share of NEWS links rather than of all posts - the more common quantity in this literature. It would require summing the alternative and mainstream columns of Table 1 (Twitter roughly 24%, Reddit roughly 11%, 4chan roughly 20%) or dividing the URL counts (Twitter 129k alt vs 413k mainstream; six subreddits 76k vs 600k; /pol/ 21k vs 82k), and R8 bars cross-category sums, so I did not create those rows. Figure 4(c) plots exactly this fraction over time but prints no values. This is the single most likely point of disagreement with another extractor and an adjudicator should settle it explicitly. (b) The user-level shares in §3/Fig. 3: '80% of the users of both platforms share only URLs from mainstream news, while, 13% of Twitter users - which are likely bots - exclusively post URLs to alternative news' and 'just 5% of these users have a fraction below 0.2'. The 13% is a share of users who share ONLY alternative news, not the SHARING actor_share the schema defines (share of users who shared ANY); the 'shared any alternative news' figure would be the complement of 80%, a complement I would have to compute (barred by R8). The denominator is also only users who posted at least one of the 99 domains' URLs, not all platform users, and the values are read off a CDF. (c) Table 4's subreddit distribution (The_Donald 35.37% of all alternative-news URLs on Reddit, politics 8.21%, news 3.85%, conspiracy 3.84%, and so on) - this is concentration ACROSS SUBREDDITS of the alternative-news URLs, i.e. within the misinformation subset, and it fails R1 anyway: no share of subreddits is stated to pair with the share of URLs, so conc_group_pct cannot be filled. Tables 5-7 (top-20 domain shares within the alternative and mainstream buckets, e.g. breitbart.com 55.58% of alternative URLs in the six subreddits) are likewise within-misinformation source concentration with no group percentage, so no CONCENTRATION row is possible. (d) Table 9 and Table 10 propagation sequences ('82% of alternative URLs and 89% of mainstream news URLs' appear on only one platform; R only 33.3%; T only 44.5%; R->T->4 36.3%) and the head-of-sequence figures (six subreddits first for 51% of alternative and 59% of mainstream URLs) - these describe where a URL appeared first, not how much misinformation there was. (e) Table 8 and the Fig. 7 speed comparisons (alternative news appears faster on Twitter than the six subreddits 80% of the time, and than /pol/ 70% of the time) - timing, not prevalence. (f) All Hawkes-process influence estimates in §5 and the retweet/like means in Table 3 (341 retweets per alternative tweet, 404 per mainstream) - influence and engagement intensities with no misinformation denominator. (g) Table 2 counts (posts/comments containing a listed URL, and unique URL counts per platform) are inputs to the Table 1 percentages rather than separate estimates. Construct caveat for the adjudicator: the 'alternative' bucket is a source-reliability list dominated by hyperpartisan outlets (breitbart.com is 46-56% of it) and two state-sponsored broadcasters, so it is broad-brush 'untrustworthy source' rather than verified falsehood - defensible under this review's broad definition and under the §3 rule that a source-reliability list makes a valid ground truth, which is why borderline is false, but the composition should be visible in any pooled estimate.

rob.design: Observational multi-platform measurement, 30 June 2016 - 28 February 2017, no human subjects. Sampling frames differ by platform: Twitter is the 1% Streaming API sample (587M posts crawled) with substantial gaps from an infrastructure failure (28 Oct-2 Nov 2016, 5-16 Nov 2016, 22 Nov 2016-13 Jan 2017, 24-28 Feb 2017) that straddle the US election; Reddit is a full census of posts and comments via Pushshift (Table 1: 332M; §2.2: approximately 42M posts plus 390M comments and 300k subreddits - an internal inconsistency); 4chan is all posts on /pol/, /sp/, /int/ and /sci/ (42M) with gaps 15-16 Oct 2016, 16-25 Dec 2016 and 10-13 Jan 2017. Twitter engagement metrics were back-filled by re-crawling between March and May 2017, retrieving 83.2% of alternative and 87.7% of mainstream tweets - the authors suggest the lower alternative retrieval rate reflects deletion or account suspension after debunking, which is itself a source of downward bias. Exposure classification is entirely source-level against a 99-domain list (45 mainstream from the Alexa top 100 news sites after excluding user-generated, specialised and non-English sites; 54 alternative from Wikipedia's List of fake news websites and FakeNewsWatch plus rt.com and sputniknews.com added by the authors); the list is published at a Google Drive link. No human coding, no coders and therefore no inter-coder reliability anywhere in the paper; no item-level fact-checking. Bot activity was deliberately NOT filtered ('posting behavior from bots can affect real users' posting behavior'), and the authors note 13% of Twitter users in the data post only alternative-news URLs and are likely bots. Statistics: Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests for distributional differences, Hawkes processes for influence. Authors' own limitations: they did not account for the content of the information (textual claims, images, videos), screenshots from 4chan are invisible to a URL-based method, and they did not examine the content of the news stories shared. A 14-page conference (IMC) paper, self-described as 'an initial attempt'.
